title: Moots Has Redesigned the Routt for Modern Gravel
content:
Steamboat Springs-based Moots, the Masters of Metal, has been building the Routt since 2013, and the all-new version, announced today, reflects how much gravel has changed since then…

More Routt More Rubber

The new Routt is our large-format gravel bike, designed around a 50 mm tire with clearance for up to 57 mm. Getting there meant reworking the frame around a new 3D-printed chainstay yoke, in-house machined UDH dropouts, and a redesigned Moots carbon gravel fork with fully integrated brake routing through our in-house titanium stem. It’s the next step for the Routt, built around where gravel is now.

Chassis Details

  • A 3D-printed chainstay yoke creates room for up to a 57mm tire while maintaining clearance for up to a 48T 1x chainring.
  • Redesigned Moots carbon gravel fork with a new D-shaped steerer allows fully integrated brake routing through our Moots Ti stem for a clean, integrated front end.
  • In-house machined UDH dropouts are designed and machined in Steamboat for current and future drivetrain compatibility.
  • Broader drivetrain options include compatibility with traditional gravel drivetrains or wide-range mullet setups, giving riders more flexibility in how they build the bike.

Routt Geometry

The above geometry chart is based around a 50 mm tire, with sizing from a 50 mm, which is specced with a 52 mm top tube, up through a 60 mm with a 60.5 mm top tube. Variable head tube and seat tube angles run across the sizing range with constant 43.7 cm chainstays.

Two Models of Routt

RSL is now offered as a premium frame upgrade rather than a separate model, giving riders one platform with two distinct tubing options.

Routt

Straight-gauge 3/2.5 titanium tubing gives the standard Routt the classic Moots ride: balanced, durable, and suited to long days and mixed terrain.

  • Straight-gauge 3/2.5 titanium
  • Balanced ride feel
  • Built for all-around gravel use

Routt RSL (available early 2027)

The RSL upgrade uses ride-tuned, double-butted titanium tubing to remove weight and sharpen the feel under power. It’s aimed at riders building toward a lighter, more race-focused setup.

  • Double-butted RSL titanium tubing
  • Lower frame weight
  • Quicker, more direct feel
  • Built with performance and weight savings in mind

See more of the new Routt at Moots.
